newsitem.title: UK: British M0 money supply growth accelerates in October.
newsitem.headline: British M0 money supply growth accelerates in October.

text.p: Growth in Britain's M0 money supply accelerated to a seasonally adjusted 7.5 percent year-on-year in October from 7.0 percent in September, the Bank of England said on Monday.

City economists said the increase in the narrow measure of money supply was consistent with continued growth in consumer spending and the figures made it likely that the central bank would call for a further tightening of monetary policy.
Strong money supply growth is widely seen as a pointer to future inflation.

Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke last week yielded to Bank of England pressure and raised official interest rates a quarter of a percentage point to 6.0 percent in an effort to choke off future inflationary pressures.
M0 money supply was up 0.7 percent in October compared with the previous month.
Ciaran Barr, an economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the figures showed retail activity remained fairly strong.
"It supports the idea that the recovery is going to continue," he said.
Separately, the Department of Environment said the number of new houses started in the three months to September rose 16 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis from the previous three months.
The housing market is an important barometer of economic confidence in this nation of home-owners.
